title: Analogy method
lines: - Make a precise sentence linking the stem pair.
- Test each option in the same sentence, in the same order.
- Two fit? Tighten the sentence and test again.
! Same topic is not same relationship.

title: Analogy traps
lines: ! Reversed order: WHOLE : PART does not match PART : WHOLE.
! Degree must move the same way: mild to strong, or strong to mild.
! Prefer links that are always true (lung : breathe), not loose associations (rose : red).
- Match parts of speech: NOUN : VERB with noun : verb.

title: Prefixes
lines: | in-, im-, il-, ir- | not | illegal, irregular

title: Suffixes show word class
lines: ! The synonym should be the same word class as the stem.

title: Confusing pairs 1
lines: | principal | main; head of a school

title: Tricky opposites
lines: - Opposite of the noun zenith (highest point): nadir.

title: Synonym groups
lines: | very large | enormous, colossal, immense, vast

title: Synonym and antonym method
lines: - Use the word in your own sentence.
- Predict a meaning (or its opposite) before reading options.
- Match strength and tone: colossal is stronger than big.
! In antonym items, one wrong option is usually a synonym.

title: Context clue signals
lines: | but, although, however, yet, despite | contrasts
| and, also, moreover | continues the idea
| because, so, therefore | follows from a cause
| such as, that is, a colon | is defined nearby
! Hardly, rarely and not reverse the meaning.

title: Tense rules for blanks
lines: | since, for (still true) | present perfect | has lived since 2019
| by next year | future perfect | will have finished
| yesterday, ago | simple past | left two days ago
| by the time (past) | past perfect | had left before we came

title: Conditionals
lines: | Real future | If + present, will + verb
| Unreal present | If + past, would + verb
| Unreal past | If + had + past participle, would have + past participle
> If he had studied, he would have passed.

title: Agreement rules
lines: - Each, every, either, neither take a singular verb: Each of the boys is here.
- Either/neither … or/nor: the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
- Collective nouns (team, committee) take a singular verb when the group acts as one unit: The team has won.
- "The number of" is singular; "a number of" is plural.

title: Verb patterns
lines: | Followed by -ing | Followed by to + verb
| enjoy, avoid, finish | want, decide, hope
| suggest, mind, deny | agree, refuse, plan
- After modals use the base verb: must go, can swim.
- Look forward to + -ing: look forward to meeting you.

title: Prepositions
lines: | prefer X to Y | prefer X than Y

title: Articles
lines: - a before a consonant sound: a university, a one-way road.
- an before a vowel sound: an hour, an honest man, an MBA.
- the for something already known or unique: the sun, the Indus.

title: Two-blank strategy
lines: - Start with the blank that has the clearer clue.
- Cross out options whose word fails there.
- Test the survivors in the other blank.
! One right word and one wrong word = wrong option.

title: Comprehension question types
lines: | Main idea | covers the whole passage
| Detail | find and match the line
| Inference | must follow from the text
| Tone | check opinion words; usually moderate
| Purpose | ask why the sentence is there

title: Eliminating options
lines: - Extreme words: always, never, only, completely.
- True in life but not stated in the passage.
- Uses passage words but reverses their meaning.
! The passage wins over your own opinion.
